- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to capture mean reversion.
- Overshoots after price spikes (especially >75% of recent high) are common; apply downward correction by 5–15% of the spike magnitude.
- Model tends to lag in downward corrections; if sentiment turns negative after a peak, adjust forecast to reflect earlier-than-expected decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out extreme deviations using 5-day moving average of sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with cycle phase; align forecast with sentiment trend direction, not just magnitude.
